## Design principles

The pipeline is built on a few principles, shared with the European MLOps framework produced within the AIML4OS project [@aiml4os2025]:

- **Separate data, code and compute.**
  - Data lives in S3 object storage, in Parquet format.
  - Code lives in Git.
  - Compute is provided by containers that are started on demand.
- **Make everything reproducible.**
  - Every training run is driven by a configuration file.
  - Every environment is pinned (uv lock files, Docker images).
  - Every dataset, model and image is versioned.
- **Package the model and its preprocessing together**, so that what was evaluated is exactly what is served (no training/serving skew).
- **Describe deployments declaratively.** The state of each environment is a set of manifests in Git, and a GitOps controller reconciles the cluster with them.
- **Keep the human in the loop.** Low-confidence predictions go to human coders, and human annotation is what measures quality.

## The platform

All development, training and pre-production work runs on **SSP Cloud**, the data science platform of the French official statistical system. SSP Cloud is built on the open-source [Onyxia](https://www.onyxia.sh/) project [@avouac2025springer]. This is possible because Sirene activity descriptions are not sensitive data.

| Component | Tool | Role in the pipeline |
|---|---|---|
| Object storage | MinIO (S3 API) | Raw extractions, cleaned datasets, splits, tokenizers, model artifacts, annotation exports |
| Interactive environments | Onyxia (VS Code, Jupyter) | Exploration and development |
| Orchestration | Argo Workflows | Batch jobs for data preparation and training on GPU nodes (A2, H100) |
| Experiment tracking and registry | MLflow | Parameters, metrics, figures and datasets for every run; versioned models |
| Serving | FastAPI on Kubernetes | REST API exposing the model |
| Continuous delivery | GitHub Actions, Argo CD | Building Docker images; GitOps synchronisation of the cluster |
| Annotation | Label Studio | Expert annotation campaigns |
| LLM inference | vLLM (OpenAI-compatible API) | Offline relabelling ([NAF 2025](data.qmd#sec-naf2025)), auditing and synthetic data ([GRAAL](data.qmd#sec-graal)) |

: Technical stack. {#tbl-stack}

Production runs on INSEE's internal Kubernetes infrastructure. The model is promoted there once it has been qualified on a pre-production platform that matches production.

## Repositories

The code is organised as a set of single-purpose repositories under the [InseeFrLab](https://github.com/InseeFrLab) GitHub organisation:

| Repository | Produces | Consumes |
|---|---|---|
| [codif-ape-nace-revision](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/codif-ape-nace-revision) | NAF 2025 labels for the training data, recoded by LLMs | Sirene extractions, correspondence table, explanatory notes, expert annotations |
| [codif-ape-preprocess](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/codif-ape-preprocess) | Cleaned and augmented training data; train/validation/test splits; an audit journal of every label change | Raw Sirene extractions, relabelled NAF 2025 data, reference tables |
| [codif-ape-train](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/codif-ape-train) | A trained model packaged as an MLflow `pyfunc`, with its metrics and diagnostic figures | Splits produced by `preprocess`; [torchTextClassifiers](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/torchTextClassifiers) |
| [codif-ape-api](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/codif-ape-api) | A Docker image of the REST API | A registered MLflow model, loaded at start-up |
| [codif-ape-cd](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/codif-ape-cd) | Kubernetes manifests for every service (APIs, dashboard, annotation ETLs, review apps) | Docker images; model names and versions |
| [torchTextClassifiers](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/torchTextClassifiers) | A generic PyTorch library for text classification (on PyPI) | — |
| [GRAAL](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/GRAAL) | LLM agents for coding, auditing and generating labels; review apps | The classification graph (Neo4j), explanatory notes, the production API |
| [codif-ape-prez](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/codif-ape-prez) | [Presentations and papers](https://inseefrlab.github.io/codif-ape-prez/) | — |

: Repositories and their contracts. {#tbl-repos}

The repositories do not import one another. They communicate through **artifacts**:

- `preprocess` publishes the location of the latest dataset, along with the feature lists, in a shared configuration file on S3, and `train` reads it.
- `train` logs a self-contained model in MLflow, which embeds its own inference code.
- `api` downloads that model at start-up, using a model name and version given as environment variables.
- `cd` decides which image, and which model version, each environment runs.

So moving a new model to an environment is a one-line change to a manifest, and it can be reviewed like any other code change.

## End-to-end flow

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-flow
%%| fig-cap: "Data and model flow across repositories."
flowchart LR
  subgraph SRC["Sources"]
    SIR["Sirene extractions"]
    ANN["Expert annotations<br/>(Label Studio)"]
    LLM["LLM relabelling<br/>(codif-ape-nace-revision, vLLM)"]
  end
  subgraph PRE["codif-ape-preprocess"]
    RUL["Rule engine<br/>+ audit journal"]
    SPL["Splits<br/>train / val / test"]
  end
  subgraph TRN["codif-ape-train"]
    TTC["torchTextClassifiers<br/>(Lightning, GPU)"]
    EVAL["Evaluation<br/>calibration, levels 1–5"]
  end
  REG[("MLflow<br/>registry")]
  subgraph SRV["Serving"]
    IMG["codif-ape-api<br/>Docker image"]
    GIT["codif-ape-cd<br/>manifests"]
    K8S["Kubernetes<br/>(Argo CD)"]
  end
  SIR --> RUL
  LLM --> RUL
  ANN --> RUL
  RUL --> SPL --> TTC --> EVAL --> REG
  REG -->|"model name + version"| K8S
  IMG --> K8S
  GIT --> K8S
  K8S -->|"predictions, logs"| MON["Monitoring<br/>dashboard"]
  MON -->|"samples to annotate"| ANN
```

Each block is described in its own chapter:

- [Data](data.qmd): sources, label cleaning and the NAF 2025 revision.
- [Data](data.qmd) also covers GRAAL, the LLM agents that audit and propose labels offline.
- [Model](model.qmd): architecture, torchTextClassifiers and training.
- [Evaluation](evaluation.qmd): which metrics, on which data.
- [Serving and deployment](serving.qmd): packaging, the API and GitOps.
- [Monitoring and annotation](monitoring.qmd): closing the loop.
- [Retraining protocol](retraining.qmd): how the loop turns into a new model, safely.
- [Organisational and infrastructural challenges](organisation.qmd): who does what, and the qualification platform.
